_meta.name: Decenza barista brain — starter knowledge base
_meta.purpose: Populated starter data for the perception->cause lexicon, causal lever graph, diagnostic rules, trace signatures, and goal->dial maps. Every fact carries provenance {source_id, tier, confidence, contested, note}. Extend by adding rows, not by rewriting logic.

tiers.T3: community or press (hypothesis / soft number only)

rails: R1 no refractometer: never emit an EY% or TDS% number; reason about direction only
R2 grind scale uncalibrated: reason in relative steps, never microns
R3 no water/PSD assay unless user reports it
R4 one untrained adapting palate: scale confidence with corroboration
R5 grind number is grinder-specific: never transfer between setups
_meta.note: Representative, not exhaustive. Numbers like '2 steps' and '~3-5s' are relative heuristics to be re-anchored per grinder/bean (R2/R5).

interactions: mechanism claim: late in the shot the puck erodes and loses resistance; holding 9 bar over an eroded bed drives late channeling and harsh/astringent tail liquid; a declining tail matches falling resistance

diagnostics.likely_cause: global under-extraction (too coarse)
diagnostics.change: grind 2 steps finer, hold dose & ratio
diagnostics.hypothesis: shot runs ~3-5s longer, flow slower; sourness drops, sweetness up
diagnostics.falsifier: if bitter/dry, overshot -> back off 1 step; if time unchanged & still sour, look at temp/water

conditions.trace: jagged / early flow spike / erratic between shots

diagnostics.likely_cause: channeling (simultaneously under & over-extracted)
diagnostics.change: fix puck prep (WDT/level/tamp), re-pull; do NOT just grind finer
diagnostics.hypothesis: trace smooths & repeats; harsh+sour edge drops together
diagnostics.falsifier: if still jagged, suspect grinder PSD or basket, not prep ritual

diagnostics.likely_cause: under-temperature
diagnostics.change: raise temp ~1-2C (gentle first nudge)
diagnostics.hypothesis: sourness eases slightly without regrinding
diagnostics.falsifier: if no change, temperature was not the driver -> grind finer

provenance.note: effect modest but real; safer than regrinding

diagnostics.likely_cause: inherent light-roast acidity (may not be a fault)
diagnostics.change: ask intent: keep as brightness, or round it -> grind finer / longer ratio / +1-2C
diagnostics.hypothesis: if rounding: acidity softens, sweetness rises
diagnostics.falsifier: if it goes flat/muddy, pushed extraction too far for this bean

provenance.note: light roasts intrinsically acidic

diagnostics.likely_cause: global over-extraction (too fine)
diagnostics.change: grind 2 steps coarser, hold dose & ratio
diagnostics.hypothesis: shot runs faster; bitterness drops, clarity up
diagnostics.falsifier: if it turns sour/thin, overshot -> back off 1 step

diagnostics.likely_cause: channeling (harsh, drying)
diagnostics.change: fix puck prep, re-pull
diagnostics.hypothesis: harshness/dryness drops as trace smooths
diagnostics.falsifier: if unchanged, look at roast/temperature

provenance.note: astringency blamed on over-extraction is typically channeling

diagnostics.likely_cause: roast-inherent bitterness (phenylindanes)
diagnostics.change: lower temp and/or coarser and/or shorter ratio
diagnostics.hypothesis: bitterness eases; body preserved
diagnostics.falsifier: if it goes sour/thin, we backed off too far

diagnostics.likely_cause: dilution (ratio too long)
diagnostics.change: shorten ratio (less water out), hold dose & grind
diagnostics.hypothesis: stronger, fuller cup; extraction roughly held
diagnostics.falsifier: if it turns sour, we also lost extraction -> grind finer

diagnostics.likely_cause: under-extraction (too coarse/fast)
diagnostics.change: grind finer, hold dose & ratio
diagnostics.hypothesis: slower shot, more body & sweetness
diagnostics.falsifier: if bitter, overshot

diagnostics.likely_cause: uneven extraction / wide grind distribution / channeling
diagnostics.change: improve prep (deep WDT); if persistent, suspect grinder uniformity
diagnostics.hypothesis: 'missing middle' fills in; sweetness & clarity rise
diagnostics.falsifier: if unchanged after clean prep, it's grinder PSD -> grinder is the limit

provenance.note: extraction spectrum

diagnostics.likely_cause: high water alkalinity buffering acidity, or staleness, or too-high strength
diagnostics.change: check days-off-roast; if fresh & clean, ask about water (alkalinity) - R3
diagnostics.hypothesis: on softer/lower-alkalinity water, clarity & brightness return
diagnostics.falsifier: if beans are stale, water is not the cause -> fresher beans

diagnostics.likely_cause: strength too high (over-concentrated) or over-extracted
diagnostics.change: lengthen ratio slightly (more water) and/or coarsen
diagnostics.hypothesis: cleaner, less muddy, still full
diagnostics.falsifier: if it thins out & sours, we went too far

diagnostics.likely_cause: Dense light-roast puck not fully saturated during pre-infusion; full pressure arrived on a partly-dry bed and ran preferential paths → uneven, under-extracted, sharp cup
diagnostics.change: Extend and soften pre-infusion before touching grind: set the PI frame to exit on pressure (~3–4 bar) rather than a short fixed time, or add ~5 s at low flow (~2–4 ml/s). One change only.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Next shot: pressure builds smoothly out of PI (no gush), sourness drops, body fills out slightly
diagnostics.falsifier: If the trace still gushes after a verified-saturated PI, saturation wasn't the cause — go one relative grind step finer (or check prep) instead. If the cup turns hollow/flat, the PI is now too long — back off half the added time.

provenance.note: high-flow→low-flow PI with modest pressure buildup
light roasts are the hard-to-wet case

diagnostics.likely_cause: Dark roast (porous, fast-wetting, degassing) over-softened by a long or high-pressure pre-infusion; puck loses structure, bleeds pressure, and over-extracts bitter
diagnostics.change: Shorten/soften pre-infusion for this bean: reduce the PI frame by ~3–5 s or lower its exit-pressure trigger ~1 bar; never run a bloom-type pause on a dark roast.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Pressure holds better through the shot; bitterness recedes without losing body
diagnostics.falsifier: If bitterness persists with a clean trace and normal timing, PI wasn't the cause — route to temperature-down or grind-coarser diagnostics.

provenance.note: blooming contraindicated on dark roasts: over-extraction, bitterness

diagnostics.likely_cause: Puck erosion under a flat 9-bar wall: the final third channels through the softened bed, adding harsh/astringent tail liquid while the front of the shot is fine
diagnostics.change: Add a declining tail frame: after the hold, decline from ~9 to ~5–6 bar over the last third of the shot. Do NOT coarsen grind for this symptom — that would fix the tail by breaking the start.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Finish cleans up (less harsh/drying) with sweetness and early-shot balance unchanged
diagnostics.falsifier: If harshness persists with the decline in place and a clean trace, the cause is global over-extraction — route to grind/temperature diagnostics. If the cup turns hollow, the decline is too deep — raise the floor to ~6–7 bar.

provenance.note: unblinded practitioner validation only

diagnostics.likely_cause: Pressure spike past ~9.5–10 bar (typically a flow frame reacting to a fine grind) compacted the puck — secondary compression → channeling → flat, muted cup
diagnostics.change: Cap the spike in the profile: add a ≤9 bar stop-limit to the offending flow frame (or convert it to a pressure frame), and/or slow the ramp. One change only.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Spike disappears from the trace; aroma and definition return next shot
diagnostics.falsifier: If the trace is capped and clean but the cup is still muted, the profile wasn't the cause — check bean freshness/temperature via existing diagnostics.

provenance.note: compaction physics above the flow peak
11 atm static shots scored worst — high pressure is not more quality

diagnostics.likely_cause: Balance acceptable, trace clean, but texture thin — the extraction levers are already at their sweet spot, so the residual body gap belongs to the profile (and/or ratio)
diagnostics.change: Run a lever-style decline as an A/B: peak ~8–9 bar then decline to ~5–6 bar, with a modest low-flow PI. Keep grind/dose/ratio fixed so the comparison is honest.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Perceived body/syrup increases over 2–3 shots with balance unchanged
diagnostics.falsifier: If body doesn't move after 2–3 shots, the profile isn't the lever here — tighten ratio (less yield) instead. NOTE contested: single-rig data suggests longer PI can REDUCE mouthfeel, so if body drops, shorten the PI component first.

provenance.note: lever-emulation body claim is community attribution
counter-signal on PI vs mouthfeel

diagnostics.likely_cause: Bright/sharp light roast still under-extracting with grind already at its practical limit (finer chokes or spikes pressure) — a grind-shaped dead end that a profile change can route around
diagnostics.change: Switch archetype instead of forcing grind: EITHER (a) extend PI to full saturation and add a gentle decline (keeps espresso concentration), OR (b) go allongé — coarsen 2–3 relative steps, cap flow higher (~3–4 ml/s), run a longer ratio (~1:3+). Pick (a) for body-forward, (b) for clarity/fruit-forward.
diagnostics.hypothesis: Acidity rounds and sweetness rises without the choke/spike behavior that blocked further grind moves
diagnostics.falsifier: If (b) turns hollow or papery, the ratio ran too long — pull the stop-weight back. If (a) still reads sour with a saturated PI and clean trace, raise temperature (~+1–2°C) via existing diagnostics.

diagnostics.likely_cause: Recurring channel breaches ACROSS shots despite verified prep (WDT, level tamp, clean basket) — the profile is applying pressure faster than this puck can consolidate

diagnostics.hypothesis: Channel signatures (notches/surges) stop recurring; bitterness and shot-to-shot variance drop
diagnostics.falsifier: If channels persist under the gentle profile, the cause is upstream of the profile — grinder clumping, basket, or distribution technique; do NOT keep softening the profile to mask it (compensation ceiling).

provenance.note: long PI + lower flat pressure as channeling mitigation in competition practice

trace_signatures.signature: Pressure overshoots sharply past ~9.5–10 bar at the start of the extraction ramp (especially in a flow-type frame), then flow collapses
trace_signatures.meaning: Profile-grind mismatch in flow mode: pressure responds to roughly the square of puck resistance, so a slightly fine grind spikes pressure; the spike compacts the puck (secondary compression) → channeling and a muted, flat cup.
trace_signatures.next_change: Cap it in the profile: convert the frame to pressure-type with a ≤9 bar limit, add a pressure stop-limit to the flow frame, or slow the ramp (longer rise time). Alternatively coarsen one relative step. Distinguish from a pure grind fault: if the cup is bitter AND the whole shot ran slow, grind is the lever; if the cup is muted and the spike is the only anomaly, the profile cap is the lever.

provenance.note: flow-mode spike → secondary compression → severe channeling, muted flavor
pressure ∝ square of resistance change in flow mode; adaptive profile designed to prevent exactly this
poroelastic compaction above ~8 bar

trace_signatures.signature: In a flow-capped frame, measured flow never reaches the cap for the whole shot; pressure sits pinned at its stop-limit
trace_signatures.meaning: The puck is too resistive for this profile (grind too fine, or dose too high, FOR this profile) — the profile is not actually flow-profiling, it has degraded into a flat pressure shot at the limiter.
trace_signatures.next_change: Coarsen one relative grind step (or lower dose slightly) so the flow target becomes reachable — OR, if the cup already tastes right, accept it and simplify to a pressure profile. This trace protects the profile from blame: the frames are fine, the resistance is wrong.

provenance.note: flow targets are only real when the machine can hold them against puck resistance

trace_signatures.signature: During a hold or decline frame, pressure falls distinctly faster than the profile commands while flow rises
trace_signatures.meaning: Puck resistance collapsing faster than expected — too coarse for this profile, an eroding/fragile puck, or dark-roast softening. Cup often thin/sour (fast total flow) or harsh at the tail (erosion channels).
trace_signatures.next_change: If the shot also ran fast and sour → grind finer (grind fault, not profile). If timing was normal but the tail bled and the finish is harsh → raise the decline's floor (e.g. end at 6 bar instead of 4) or add a flow stop-limit to the tail frame. A gentle, commanded decline that tracks the profile is healthy — only uncommanded bleed is a fault.

provenance.note: puck breakdown late in shot
curve volatility diagnostics on the DE1

trace_signatures.signature: Near-zero flow well into the extraction phase, then a sudden flow surge with an abrupt pressure drop
trace_signatures.meaning: An over-resistive puck held back the water until a channel blew through — after the breach, most water transits the channel. Classic combined fault: usually grind-too-fine or a prep defect, detonated by the pressure the profile applied.
trace_signatures.next_change: Prep gate first (priority 1): distribution/WDT/tamp, then coarsen if it was choking. Only AFTER prep is verified, a gentler profile (longer low-flow PI, peak ≤8 bar, slower ramp) reduces recurrence. Never use the profile to hide this trace — that is the compensation ceiling.

provenance.note: uneven-extraction physics

trace_signatures.signature: Flat 9-bar profile: pressure holds fine, but flow accelerates steadily through the final third of the shot
trace_signatures.meaning: The puck is eroding under constant pressure; late liquid is increasingly fast, dilute, and channel-prone — the component community practice associates with a harsh/astringent finish. This is a fault grind cannot fix without wrecking the shot's start.
trace_signatures.next_change: Add a declining tail: after the hold, insert a pressure frame declining from ~9 to ~5–6 bar over the last third of the shot (or a flow stop-limit on the final frame). Hypothesis: finish cleans up with the start unchanged.

provenance.note: ramp-down rationale
decline phase of the 3-phase model

trace_signatures.signature: Pressure peaks at ~8–9 bar then declines smoothly and monotonically while flow stays steady or drifts gently up; no notches or surges
trace_signatures.meaning: Healthy shot shape for a decline-type profile: resistance falling gradually and the profile tracking it. Not a fault — this is the reference 'good' curve the other signatures deviate from.
trace_signatures.next_change: No profile change. If taste is still off with this trace, the fault is an extraction lever (grind/ratio/temp) or the bean — route to existing diagnostics.

provenance.note: peak-then-gentle-decline described as the near-universal resistance evolution

goals.goal: Tame a bright/sharp light roast (keep it interesting, lose the sting)
goals.target_region: Acidity rounded into sweetness; trace shows full saturation before ramp (no post-PI gush)
goals.default_path: Extend PI to a pressure-exit trigger (~3–4 bar) so the dense puck fully saturates, then a gentle ramp and modest decline. If grind is already pinned at its fine limit, switch archetype (allongé, or blooming if beans and prep are excellent) instead of forcing grind.

roast_conditioned.light: As stated — this goal IS the light-roast case; temperature convention in the Decent community runs hotter for light (~92°C+) vs dark (~88°C), so pair the profile move with the existing temperature paths rather than replacing them
roast_conditioned.dark: Not applicable — a 'sour' dark roast is under-extraction: route to grind/temperature diagnostics, and do NOT extend PI (gush/bitterness risk)

goals.target_region: Distinct flavors, clean non-drying finish; trace shows capped peak (≤9 bar) and a commanded decline
goals.default_path: First remove profile faults that mute (pressure spikes past ~9.5 bar → cap them). Then add/deepen a declining tail. For maximum clarity on suitable beans, allongé (coarser + faster flow + longer ratio) — accepting the body trade-off explicitly.

roast_conditioned.light: Allongé shines here (fruity/washed/naturals); easiest archetype to dial
roast_conditioned.dark: Clarity on dark roasts is mostly a temperature-down and ratio question; profile contribution is limited to trimming the harsh tail with a decline

goals.goal: More consistency / forgiveness shot-to-shot (reduce channeling variance)
